items.definition: The overall security policy, run as a repeating Plan-Do-Check-Act cycle (ISO 27001).
items.examples: Reviewing and improving security measures every quarter.
items.examTip: PDCA = continuous improvement. Security is never finished because threats change.
keyFacts: Covers internet use, passwords, staff duties, training

items.definition: Rules for acceptable internet and email use at work.
items.examples: Banning downloads of executable files; warning that email may be monitored.
items.examTip: Covers offensive material, confidential info, copyright, risky sites and monitoring.
keyFacts: The organisation may scan traffic and keep emails

items.definition: Rules and tools that enforce strong passwords and safe account use.
items.examples: Blocking common passwords; locking accounts after failed logins.
items.examTip: Include: length/strength, no sharing, no reuse, lockout, minimum age, expiry.
keyFacts: Use technology to rely less on passwords

items.definition: What staff must do for security, and how they are trained.
items.examples: Annual security training; reporting suspicious emails.
items.examTip: Good training is funded, flexible, varied, tracked, rewarding and ongoing.
keyFacts: Staff: train, follow procedures, report suspicious activity

items.definition: A check that the organisation follows its own security policies and the law.
items.examples: Finding accounts that still belong to ex-employees.
items.examTip: Finds gaps and checks against internal policy AND external law.

items.definition: A written policy stating what is backed up, how, how often and by whom.
items.examples: Nightly incrementals, weekly fulls, quarterly restore tests.
items.examTip: A good policy includes testing restores and legal compliance.
keyFacts: What data, which method and type

items.definition: A policy making sure the organisation follows data protection law (GDPR).
items.examples: Appointing a Data Protection Officer; covering contractors too.
items.examTip: Links to GDPR. Key parts: DPO, principles, rights, training, accountability.

items.definition: The plan for how the organisation responds to a security incident.
items.examples: A triage flowchart and contact list including legal, PR, HR and insurance.
items.examTip: Stages: triage/escalate → contain, mitigate, recover → review and close.
keyFacts: Contacts: response lead, IT, management, legal, PR, HR, insurance

items.definition: A policy for restoring systems and operations after a major disruption.
items.examples: Deciding whether to trigger incident response, business continuity or full recovery.
items.examTip: Includes triage (rating severity), roles, contact lists and monitoring.
keyFacts: Triage: list events and rate severity

items.definition: A policy for using outside providers for cloud, hardware, software and support.
items.examples: A service level agreement setting response and fix times.
items.examTip: Covers authorisation, accountability, SLAs and incident handling.
keyFacts: Who authorises and who is accountable
